findings.text: test_every_store_op_verb_names_a_target compares set membership only, so a verb added to TARGET_COMPOSED_VERBS without a matching branch in _op_target_path falls through to the 'return None' at reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:1354 and the case stays green while the conflict refusal again names no target for that verb, which is the exact defect its docstring says it prevents.

The Measure paragraph says both arms are git archive extractions, but logs/head_targeted.log:5 and logs/base_targeted.log:5 record '# cwd:' as the source worktree while the command cds into the /tmp extraction, so the log's own provenance fields disagree; the extraction claim is still supported by the command and by '# module.__file__' naming the /tmp tree, but the cwd line reads as a worktree run; the reader has to reconcile two header lines.

The ruff claim (7 pre-existing findings at each arm, format clean) appears in the manifest artifacts line and in the fragment's Measure paragraph but no ruff log exists under logs/, so the receipt the done_when asks for cannot be checked by a later reader.
